OPERATION ASCEND — B2
GLOBAL PARTNER GROWTH, SALES OPERATIONS & REVENUE INTELLIGENCE
ScaleSmiths Next-Generation Partner Operating System
Organisation: ScaleSmiths Limited
Repository: https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths
Previous operation: Project AEGIS — B1.7
Next proposed stage: B2 — Operation ASCEND
Implementation branch: `feature/operation-ascend-b2`
Execution mode: Autonomous engineering with verified testing and founder-controlled release gates.
THE MISSION
ScaleSmiths has developed the technical foundation for an international independent sales partner programme.
B0 through B1.6 are merged.
B1.7 is completed in draft PR #163, pending final human review and merge.
Forge approval reliability has been addressed in draft PR #164.
A separate hydration and history-navigation fix exists on branch:
`claude/awesome-hawking-ximwzj`
Commit:
`f3e6f4d`
The previous stages created:

* Partner recruitment and onboarding.
* Versioned agreement acceptance.
* Founder administration.
* Partner Academy.
* Professional Resource Centre.
* Technical Knowledge Base.
* Objection Handling.
* Unified Partner Workspace.
* Prospect registration.
* Meeting requests.
* Commission infrastructure.
* Recognition and referral systems.
* Financial audit and concurrency safeguards.

B2 transforms this foundation into a scalable commercial operating system.
The platform should help independent partners generate business and help founders manage an expanding international sales network.
The objective is to support growth from a handful of partners to hundreds or potentially thousands without needing a proportional increase in administrative work.
This is a capacity target, not a claim that the current infrastructure supports those numbers.
Do not implement superficial dashboards.
Build genuinely functional systems backed by real data, strong permissions, appropriate automation and verified tests.
PHASE ZERO — FINISH THE EXISTING FIXES
This phase must be completed or correctly isolated before integrating B2.
0.1 Verify the repository
Fetch the latest master SHA.
Inspect:

* PR #163 — B1.7 Project AEGIS.
* PR #164 — Forge Preview Approval.
* Branch `claude/awesome-hawking-ximwzj`.
* Current CI and CodeQL.
* Current branch protection.
* Active worktrees.
* Migration history.
* Relevant repository instructions.

Do not assume the old state remains current.
Do not overwrite or duplicate work.
0.2 Complete the hydration fix
Inspect commit `f3e6f4d`.
Verify that the hydration marker reliably indicates that Next.js navigation is ready.
Review:

* `admin/src/app/layout.tsx`
* `admin/src/components/admin-shell/HydrationMarker.tsx`
* `admin/test/e2e/admin-workspace.spec.ts`

Run the targeted test repeatedly.
Confirm:

* History navigation before hydration is not attempted by the test.
* History navigation after hydration works.
* Normal user navigation works.
* Browser Back behaves correctly.
* Existing assertions remain unchanged.
* No arbitrary sleeps are introduced.
* No timeouts are increased.
* No unrelated production behaviour is changed.

Open a small draft PR for the fix.
Verify full CI.
0.3 Complete the Forge approval fix
Inspect PR #164.
Verify:

* Server-confirmed approval state.
* Double-click protection.
* Concurrent approval protection.
* Failed request handling.
* Stale-state regression coverage.
* Browser tests.
* CI and security checks.

Confirm the server's response is authoritative.
Do not reopen the earlier disproven root-cause hypothesis.
0.4 Finalise B1.7
Inspect PR #163.
Confirm:

* Full required CI passes.
* Database rehearsal evidence is present.
* All documented findings are accurate.
* No secrets entered the repository.
* The release decision package is complete.
* Feature flags remain disabled.

Recommend the merge order:

1. Forge reliability fix.
2. Hydration reliability fix.
3. B1.7 integration and hardening.

Do not merge without founder approval and the repository's required human review.
If B1.7 remains unmerged, build B2 from the current master and keep dependent integration work separate until the required changes land.
0.5 Operational risks
Carry these known release issues into the B2 dependency register:

* `admin.scalesmiths.co.uk` incorrectly redirects to `www.confirmakill.co.uk`.
* Canonical admin hostname remains unresolved.
* Production error monitoring is disabled.
* Production off-host backups are unverified.
* Resend configuration is incomplete.
* AP-COM-03 remains a founder decision.
* Approved partner agreement text is not yet available to the portal.
* Agreement jurisdiction binding is not enforced.
* Content approvals remain outstanding.

Do not silently mark these resolved.
The incorrect admin redirect is a security and trust concern. Propose the precise correction, but do not modify DNS without authorisation.
PHASE ONE — B2 PRODUCT ARCHITECTURE
Before coding, inspect the existing B-series roadmap, if one exists.
Confirm whether B2 already has a defined scope.
If a formally approved B2 specification exists, reconcile this directive with it rather than silently replacing it.
Otherwise adopt the following proposed B2 structure.
B2.1 — Advanced Partner Pipeline
B2.2 — Intelligent Prospect Qualification
B2.3 — Founder Sales Command Centre
B2.4 — Revenue Intelligence & Forecasting
B2.5 — Partner Performance & Development
B2.6 — Delivery Handoff & Client Lifecycle
B2.7 — Automation, Integration & Full Acceptance
Create a dependency graph.
Identify existing capabilities that can be extended rather than duplicated.
Produce a concise implementation plan, then begin engineering.
Do not stop at the planning stage.
B2.1 — ADVANCED PARTNER PIPELINE
The current platform supports prospect registration and core opportunity tracking.
B2.1 must turn this into a professional, intuitive pipeline.
Partner pipeline
Provide a visual sales pipeline based on the existing authoritative opportunity lifecycle.
Partners should be able to understand:

* Which prospects are active.
* Which require action.
* Which are awaiting founder review.
* Which meetings are pending.
* Which meetings are confirmed.
* Which opportunities are progressing.
* Which opportunities are closed or no longer viable.
* Which require further information.

Do not invent status transitions that conflict with the existing financial or ownership rules.
Views
Implement:

* Kanban-style pipeline where appropriate.
* Table view.
* Compact mobile list.
* Prospect detail.
* Search.
* Filtering.
* Sorting.

Suggested filters:

* Status.
* Assigned partner.
* Service interest.
* Last activity.
* Next action.
* Meeting status.
* Date added.

Partner access must remain limited to their own authorised opportunities.
Founder access must follow the established scope and role controls.
Pipeline interactions
Where supported by the existing state machine:

* Open an opportunity.
* Update permitted information.
* Record an interaction.
* Schedule an internal follow-up.
* Request founder assistance.
* View related meetings.
* Access contextual guidance.
* Review the opportunity's current status.

Do not allow unrestricted drag-and-drop status changes.
Any visual stage transition must call the server's authorised state transition.
If a transition is forbidden, display why.
Never let a UI gesture bypass commission eligibility or ownership checks.
Activity timeline
Create a meaningful, audit-backed timeline.
Potential entries:

* Prospect submitted.
* Founder reviewed.
* Information requested.
* Meeting requested.
* Meeting confirmed.
* Proposal prepared.
* Proposal issued.
* Contract accepted.
* Payment verified.
* Commission event recorded.

Only show events that genuinely occurred.
Do not fabricate activity to populate the interface.
Respect privacy and access restrictions.
B2.2 — INTELLIGENT PROSPECT QUALIFICATION
Build structured, deterministic qualification tools that help partners understand the needs of a business.
Do not start with an expensive AI dependency.
Qualification workspace
Support existing or approved fields such as:

* Business type.
* Location.
* Website availability.
* Current digital presence.
* Services required.
* Main business problem.
* Current supplier.
* Budget indication, where voluntarily provided.
* Desired timescale.
* Decision-maker involvement.
* Existing technical requirements.
* Additional notes.

Do not require unnecessary personal information.
Qualification assistance
Display:

* Missing discovery information.
* Suggested follow-up questions.
* Related approved Knowledge Base articles.
* Related objection responses.
* Relevant professional resources.
* Technical escalation suggestions.

Use the existing content governance rules.
Only published, current, partner-safe material may be recommended.
Qualification score
If implementing a score, make it transparent and explainable.
Use a rules-based model.
Examples:

* Clearly identified business requirement.
* Decision-maker confirmed.
* Relevant service fit.
* Requirements sufficiently documented.
* Timeline understood.
* Scope ready for founder review.

Do not imply a business is guaranteed to purchase.
Do not use protected personal characteristics.
Do not automatically reject a prospect solely because of a score.
Founders must be able to inspect the factors.
Do not let the score override ownership, approval or financial rules.
Duplicate prevention
Review the existing prospect-ownership rules.
Improve duplicate detection where necessary.
Handle:

* Same company with different spelling.
* Duplicate domains.
* Duplicate submissions.
* Concurrent registrations.
* Existing active ownership claims.

Use server-enforced constraints and review processes.
Do not expose another partner's confidential prospect records.
B2.3 — FOUNDER SALES COMMAND CENTRE
Build a practical sales operations experience for ScaleSmiths founders.
The system must help a small central team coordinate a growing international network.
Do not create a competing second CRM.
Extend the existing founder Expansion workspace.
Global pipeline overview
Display actual:

* Total active opportunities.
* Opportunities awaiting review.
* Meetings requiring confirmation.
* Opportunities requiring technical scoping.
* Proposals awaiting action.
* Confirmed commercial outcomes.
* Partner assistance requests.
* Stalled opportunities.
* Onboarding bottlenecks.

Use real source data.
Work queue
Founders should see prioritised operational tasks.
Examples:

* New prospect requiring review.
* Technical escalation.
* Meeting request.
* Missing qualification information.
* Agreement awaiting action.
* Proposal follow-up.
* Partner application requiring review.
* Notification delivery failure.

Each queue item must link to a real actionable destination.
No inert controls.
Partner oversight
Allow founders to inspect:

* Partner status.
* Partner region.
* Open opportunities.
* Confirmed outcomes.
* Outstanding help requests.
* Commission summaries.
* Operational bottlenecks.

Do not expose private learning progress without an approved policy.
Do not rank partners using hidden or unexplained rules.
Assignment and ownership
Where founders can assign a task or opportunity:

* Validate authorisation.
* Preserve ownership history.
* Record the reason.
* Prevent accidental duplicate assignments.
* Handle concurrent actions.
* Notify the relevant partner only when approved notifications are enabled.

Do not silently transfer a partner's commercial entitlement.
B2.4 — REVENUE INTELLIGENCE & FORECASTING
This stage should give ScaleSmiths useful visibility into business performance.
It must use the existing financial engine.
Do not create another source of truth.
Revenue dashboard
Provide:

* Verified collected revenue.
* Outstanding invoiced amounts.
* Recognised commission liabilities.
* Paid commissions.
* Retainer revenue.
* One-off build revenue.
* Revenue by service.
* Revenue by period.
* Relevant partner-attributed revenue.
* Pipeline opportunity value where supported.

Clearly distinguish collected revenue from projected revenue.
Never show forecast values as money earned.
Forecasting
Build a transparent forecast model.
Suggested inputs:

* Qualified active opportunities.
* Historical conversion rates.
* Existing contractual amounts.
* Contracted recurring fees.
* Known cancellation or refund events.
* Approved pipeline stage assumptions.

Use real historical data where available.
If insufficient data exists, say so.
Do not invent historical conversion rates.
Forecast scenarios
Support:

* Conservative.
* Baseline.
* Optimistic.

Every scenario must disclose its assumptions.
Allow founders to adjust hypothetical values without changing accounting records.
Use clearly separated forecast tables or views.
Do not write forecasts to the financial ledger.
Partner commission visibility
Partners should be able to understand:

* Eligible commission.
* Earned commission.
* Pending commission.
* Adjustments.
* Withdrawals.
* Historical transactions.

Use the existing approved definitions.
Preserve the £705 example as an illustrative standard acquisition, not a promise.
Do not change the 30% rate or other commercial logic without explicit founder authorisation.
B2.5 — PARTNER PERFORMANCE & DEVELOPMENT
Build fair, useful performance visibility that helps partners improve their results.
This is intended for independent contractors.
It must not create an employee-style performance management system.
Personal performance
Partners may view:

* Their own registered prospects.
* Meetings requested.
* Meetings confirmed.
* Qualified opportunities.
* Completed sales.
* Verified earned commissions.
* Relevant achievement milestones.

Avoid compulsory quotas or attendance requirements.
Development insights
Offer optional insights such as:

* Common objections encountered.
* Services generating interest.
* Missing qualification information.
* Frequently used approved resources.
* Voluntarily completed learning.
* Suggested material for a partner's next opportunity.

Do not disclose learning progress to founders unless the privacy decision permits it.
Do not make Academy completion a condition of commission.
Recognition
Integrate existing recognition and achievement systems.
Do not invent new monetary bonuses.
Any paid recognition event must use the existing approved commercial engine.
Performance metrics
Every metric should have:

* A clear definition.
* An authoritative data source.
* An appropriate time period.
* Correct access controls.
* Reliable empty states.

No fabricated leaderboards.
No unsupported earnings predictions.
No comparison of partners without explicit permission and privacy review.
B2.6 — DELIVERY HANDOFF & CLIENT LIFECYCLE
ScaleSmiths' sales process must connect cleanly to actual service delivery.
This is particularly important as international partners bring in more clients.
Handoff workflow
When a prospect becomes an authorised client engagement, create a structured delivery handoff using the existing systems.
Include:

* Client business.
* Approved service scope.
* Accepted proposal or contract reference.
* Commercial terms.
* Technical requirements.
* Project contacts.
* Key deadlines.
* Outstanding questions.
* Assigned delivery owner.
* Related opportunity.
* Relevant approved documents.

Do not create a real delivery commitment from an unapproved prospect.
Founder controls
The founder should be able to:

* Review a proposed handoff.
* Request clarification.
* Approve the handoff.
* Assign delivery responsibility.
* Track handoff status.
* Review missing requirements.

Preserve audit history.
Delivery status
Partners should have appropriate read-only visibility into the status of opportunities they introduced.
Do not expose internal engineering notes, credentials, confidential technical systems or unrelated client information.
Integrate existing project systems
Inspect whether existing Forge or other ScaleSmiths delivery tooling offers an appropriate integration boundary.
Do not tightly couple the partner programme to Forge internal implementation details.
Use a documented interface or existing shared contract.
If no safe integration exists, implement an independent, reviewable handoff interface rather than invasive cross-product changes.
B2.7 — CONTROLLED AUTOMATION & ACCEPTANCE
Once B2's workflows exist, introduce limited automation that genuinely reduces manual administration.
Automation examples

* Detect opportunities awaiting founder review.
* Highlight follow-ups due.
* Identify expired meeting requests.
* Flag incomplete qualification.
* Surface pending handoffs.
* Identify failed notification delivery.
* Highlight approved content approaching review expiry.
* Summarise operational bottlenecks.

Do not send automatic messages to clients without approval.
Do not automatically approve contracts.
Do not automatically activate partners.
Do not automatically create commission.
Do not automatically move money.
Do not automatically assign ownership where contractual entitlement may be affected.
Automation architecture
Use existing scheduled jobs and notification infrastructure where possible.
Require:

* Idempotency.
* Explicit state checks.
* Bounded retries.
* Failure visibility.
* Audit trails.
* Rate limits.
* Safe defaults.
* Feature flags.
* Clear ownership.

Avoid introducing a complex agent framework for simple deterministic workflows.
Future AI integration
Design extension points for future AI assistance, including the eventual TITAN OS architecture.
Potential future uses:

* Prospect research.
* Sales conversation preparation.
* Opportunity summaries.
* Proposal drafting.
* Technical scoping assistance.
* Partner support triage.
* Delivery handoff preparation.

For B2, establish secure interfaces rather than autonomous production agents.
Any future AI action must follow:

* Least privilege.
* Human approval for consequential changes.
* Auditable actions.
* Tenant isolation.
* Explicit budget limits.
* Verified source material.
* No unauthorised external communications.

Do not introduce paid model usage without approval.
PHASE TWO — VISUAL & INTERACTION STANDARD
All B2 features must feel native to the existing ScaleSmiths design system.
Design direction:

* Premium dark interface.
* Metallic gold.
* Silver.
* Clear information hierarchy.
* Restrained animations.
* Responsive tables.
* Comfortable spacing.
* Useful hover states.
* Strong focus states.
* Fast navigation.
* Readable charts.
* Polished empty states.

Required interaction quality
Test:

* Every button.
* Every menu.
* Every tab.
* Every dropdown.
* Every filter.
* Every search.
* Every form.
* Every pipeline interaction.
* Every modal.
* Every status change.
* Every copy action.
* Every navigation control.

No placeholder buttons.
No dead links.
No misleading state changes.
No fabricated numbers.
Responsive tests
Test at:

* 320px.
* 390px.
* 768px.
* 1024px.
* 1440px.
* 1920px.

Use actual browser screenshots.
Inspect the images.
Test keyboard navigation.
Respect reduced motion.
Use WCAG 2.2 AA as the accessibility target.
Do not rely solely on axe.
PHASE THREE — SECURITY & DATA ISOLATION
B2 introduces more commercially sensitive views.
Test the full role matrix.
Roles

* Anonymous.
* Applicant.
* Active partner.
* Suspended partner.
* Revoked partner.
* Founder.
* Other existing authorised roles.

Critical boundaries
Partner A must not access Partner B's:

* Prospects.
* Opportunities.
* Meetings.
* Notes.
* Revenue.
* Commission.
* Private activity.
* Agreements.
* Client information.
* Delivery records.

Founder-only analytics must be protected server-side.
No UI-only authorisation.
Threat review
Test:

* IDOR.
* SQL injection.
* Cross-partner data leakage.
* Forged status transitions.
* Concurrent assignments.
* Duplicate prospect submissions.
* Tampered monetary values.
* Unauthorised opportunity transfer.
* Unsafe note rendering.
* Excessive information in logs.
* Unbounded analytics queries.
* Notification abuse.

Use disposable test environments.
Do not run destructive security tests against production.
PHASE FOUR — DATABASE ENGINEERING
Reuse the existing database architecture.
Before introducing a table or migration, determine whether the information already exists.
Prefer derived views and existing audit events where appropriate.
For necessary new data:

* Add forward-only migrations.
* Preserve historical records.
* Use appropriate foreign keys.
* Enforce ownership and state constraints.
* Apply restricted-role permissions.
* Add indexes justified by real query patterns.
* Document retention.
* Test concurrent writes.
* Include idempotency.

Verify PostgreSQL 14 compatibility.
Do not run production migrations.
Do not modify financial ledger architecture without approval.
PHASE FIVE — FULL SYSTEM ACCEPTANCE
Build complete browser journeys.
Journey A — Partner pipeline

1. Partner logs in.
2. Opens pipeline.
3. Registers a synthetic prospect.
4. Prospect appears in the correct state.
5. Partner adds permitted qualification information.
6. Contextual guidance updates.
7. Partner requests founder assistance.
8. Request appears in founder queue.
9. Founder responds.
10. Partner sees the correct outcome.
11. Commission remains unchanged.

Journey B — Founder operations

1. Founder signs in with MFA.
2. Opens the sales command centre.
3. Reviews active opportunities.
4. Filters by status.
5. Opens an escalation.
6. Reviews qualification.
7. Performs an authorised transition.
8. Audit history records the change.
9. Another partner cannot access the opportunity.

Journey C — Revenue

1. Seed synthetic invoices and verified collections.
2. Verify dashboard collected revenue.
3. Verify pending revenue is separate.
4. Verify earned commission matches the ledger.
5. Verify reversals.
6. Verify forecast assumptions.
7. Change forecast scenario.
8. Confirm no financial records change.

Journey D — Delivery handoff

1. Founder reviews a qualifying opportunity.
2. Handoff is prepared.
3. Missing scope blocks approval.
4. Founder completes required information.
5. Handoff is approved.
6. Delivery owner is assigned.
7. Partner sees permitted status.
8. Internal technical information remains private.
9. Handoff events are auditable.

Journey E — Security

1. Partner A creates an opportunity.
2. Partner B attempts direct access.
3. Access is refused.
4. Partner B attempts to change its stage.
5. Change is refused.
6. Suspended partner cannot access the pipeline.
7. Partner cannot open founder analytics.
8. Draft content remains unavailable.
9. Financial records remain unchanged by guidance interactions.

PHASE SIX — REGRESSION AND CI
Run the complete relevant test matrix.
Include:

* Admin unit.
* Web unit.
* TypeScript.
* ESLint.
* Production builds.
* Database migrations.
* PostgreSQL 14/16 compatibility.
* Financial invariants.
* Concurrency.
* Empower Browser Acceptance.
* Admin Forge E2E.
* Forge Workflow E2E.
* Security.
* CodeQL.
* Backup and Restore.
* Root Hygiene.
* Nginx Topology.
* Cross-browser Smoke.
* Public website performance budgets.

Maintain the 900 ms performance threshold.
Do not increase timeouts or disable tests to obtain green results.
For flaky tests, reproduce, diagnose and fix the underlying issue when practical.
PHASE SEVEN — DELIVERY STRATEGY
B2 is substantial.
Do not deliver one enormous unreviewable PR.
Use small, complete, independently testable vertical slices.
Recommended sequence:

1. Phase Zero reliability fixes and integration preparation.
2. B2.1 pipeline.
3. B2.2 qualification.
4. B2.3 founder operations.
5. B2.4 revenue intelligence.
6. B2.5 performance.
7. B2.6 delivery handoff.
8. B2.7 automation and acceptance.

Create a draft PR for each significant B2 slice.
Each PR requires:

* Functional implementation.
* Relevant tests.
* Database compatibility evidence.
* Browser evidence.
* Security assessment.
* CI results.
* Migration notes.
* Rollback considerations.
* Updated documentation.

Do not merge automatically.
Do not deploy automatically.
Do not activate unfinished features.
Continue into the next independent slice only when its dependencies are available.
If the entire B2 sequence cannot be completed in one execution session, deliver completed reviewable slices and accurate next-step documentation. Do not claim unfinished work is complete.
PHASE EIGHT — PRODUCTION RELEASE BOUNDARIES
Keep B1 release readiness separate from B2 development.
Gate A — Dormant code deployment
Requires:

* Human-reviewed code.
* Green CI.
* Migration rehearsal.
* Backup verification.
* Operational monitoring.
* Rollback readiness.
* Explicit founder deployment approval.

Gate B — Partner activation
Requires:

* Commercial approvals.
* Solicitor-reviewed agreement publication.
* Jurisdiction validation.
* Privacy decisions.
* Email readiness.
* Content approval.
* Operational support.
* Founder activation approval.

B2 development must not bypass these gates.
All new B2 capabilities must default OFF.
PHASE NINE — DOCUMENTATION
Create:
`docs/expansion/ascend/B2-ARCHITECTURE.md`
`docs/expansion/ascend/B2-ROADMAP.md`
`docs/expansion/ascend/B2-SECURITY-MODEL.md`
`docs/expansion/ascend/B2-ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA.md`
`docs/expansion/ascend/B2-IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md`
For every completed slice, record:

* Branch.
* PR.
* Commit.
* Implementation.
* Database changes.
* Financial impact.
* Security controls.
* Tests.
* Browser evidence.
* CI results.
* Outstanding decisions.
* Deployment status.

Use accurate completion labels.
Do not make documentation a substitute for implementation.
PHASE TEN — INDEPENDENT REVIEW
Perform a separate model review where supported.
Focus on:

* Architectural consistency.
* Authentication.
* Cross-partner isolation.
* Financial correctness.
* Ownership integrity.
* Forecast accuracy.
* Delivery handoff.
* Concurrency.
* Privacy.
* Performance.
* Accessibility.

Fix critical and high findings.
Document the remaining findings.
Model review is not human approval.
FINAL COMPLETION STANDARD
B2 engineering is complete only when:

* Phase Zero reliability work has been correctly integrated or remains explicitly isolated behind review gates.
* The pipeline is functional.
* Qualification guidance works.
* Founder sales operations are usable.
* Revenue reporting uses authoritative financial data.
* Forecasts clearly distinguish assumptions from actuals.
* Partner performance respects independent-contractor boundaries.
* Delivery handoffs preserve approvals and audit history.
* Automation is deterministic, safe and observable.
* Role isolation is tested.
* Financial invariants are preserved.
* PostgreSQL compatibility is verified.
* Browser journeys pass.
* Visual and accessibility checks pass.
* CI is green on final PR heads.
* Independent review is documented.
* All changes remain reviewable.
* No unauthorised deployment or activation occurs.

If any stage is blocked, complete the independent safe work and describe the blocker precisely.
FINAL DIRECTIVE
B1 built the partner platform.
B2 must make that platform commercially powerful.
Build a system where an independent partner can discover opportunities, qualify prospects, receive approved guidance, collaborate with founders and understand their commercial progress.
Build a system where ScaleSmiths founders can coordinate international sales activity, manage a growing pipeline, understand revenue, protect margins and oversee delivery.
Keep the financial ledger authoritative.
Keep partners independent.
Keep permissions strict.
Keep commercial decisions founder-controlled.
Keep automation safe.
Keep the interface premium.
Keep testing real.
Make the system capable of growing without requiring constant manual intervention from the founders.
OPERATION ASCEND — B2
FROM PARTNER INFRASTRUCTURE TO GLOBAL REVENUE OPERATIONS.
EXECUTE.

+import { useEffect } from "react"
+
+/**
+ * Marks <html data-scalesmiths-hydrated="true"> once React has hydrated the app.
+ * The Next.js app router (an ancestor) patches window.history in its own effects,
+ * which have run by the time this marker appears. Browser tests wait for this
+ * signal before driving client-only behaviour such as history.pushState, matching
+ * the public web app's convention.
+ */
+export function HydrationMarker() {
+  useEffect(() => {
+    document.documentElement.dataset.scalesmithsHydrated = "true"
+    return () => {
+      delete document.documentElement.dataset.scalesmithsHydrated
+    }
+  }, [])
+
+  return null

# Implementation roadmap

## A: foundation

1. Audit source, record baseline and preserve unrelated dirty instruction files.
2. Document architecture, security, data and financial contracts before substantial code.
3. Public recruitment, calculator, validated gated applications and founder review.
4. Extend existing identity with invitation/activation and restrictive partner role.
5. Canonical prospect registration, confidential duplicates, discovery and scope review.
6. Capacity reservations and immutable accepted commercial terms.
7. Verified collection events, versioned commission, adjustments, manual payout and reconciliation.
8. Founder and partner workflows, published resources and real empty states.
9. Production-code security/financial tests, isolated DB workflow and browser evidence.

## B: intelligence (deferred until A acceptance)

Isolated SSRF-resistant website audits, approved Sales Studio projections, knowledge search, budgeted AI and support escalation. No simulated working provider.

## C: velocity (deferred)

Authoritative provider payment events, invoice matching, durable notifications and delivery handover automation. No autonomous transfers.

## D: national scale (deferred)

Attribution optimisation, regional insights and advanced analytics only after validated operational demand.

## Acceptance

The 30-step requested journey must reconcile exactly £705 from £1,000 + £1,000 + £350 net collections, survive replay/concurrency and deny cross-partner access. Incomplete journey steps are reported explicitly in STATUS.md. No placeholder counts as complete.

/**
 * Operation Empower B1.6: deterministic, explainable mapping from what a partner has already recorded about a prospect to approved
 * guidance. Pure: no database, no network, no logging, no generated text.
 *
 * Privacy: prospect text only decides which rule applies. The search terms used afterwards come from the fixed vocabulary below,
 * never from what the partner or client typed, so prospect details never reach a search query, a log or another partner.
 */
import { DISCOVERY_FIELDS } from "./expansion"
import { COURSE_CATEGORIES, KNOWLEDGE_TOPICS } from "./empower-content"

type KnowledgeTopic = (typeof KNOWLEDGE_TOPICS)[number]
type CourseCategory = (typeof COURSE_CATEGORIES)[number]
export type DiscoveryRecord = Partial<Record<(typeof DISCOVERY_FIELDS)[number], string>>

export type GuidanceRule = {
  id: string
  /** Shown to the partner: why this guidance appears. Never quotes the prospect's own words. */
  reason: string
  knowledgeTopics: KnowledgeTopic[]
  courseCategories: CourseCategory[]
  /** Fixed vocabulary for resource search; founders change it by code review. */
  searchTerms: string[]
  /** B1.5 objection categories, used once objection handling is merged and switched on. */
  objectionCategories: string[]
  escalation?: "technical_scoping" | "bespoke_discovery" | "commercial_assistance"
  when: (d: DiscoveryRecord, p: { website: boolean }) => boolean

result.output:
## Summary

Fixes the intermittent Admin Forge E2E failure in test 16 ("approves the preview through the existing project action") by fixing the product, not the test. After "Internally approve preview", the next action ("Record client approval") was derived only from the page's server-rendered props, so it appeared only after a complete server re-render of the Forge project page reached the browser. The PATCH that records the approval had already committed and returned the persisted project, but the interface ignored that response. When the re-render was slow, the page kept offering an approval that had already been recorded. The workspace now advances on the server's own confirmation. A compare-and-set also closes a latent double-approval defect that the investigation uncovered.

## Root cause and evidence

- **CI signature:** test 16 failed on unrelated commits `62c106c` and `964eb2c` ([#163](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/163)) with "Record client approval" not visible after the 10 s expectation, in 11.1 s. It passed on re-run.
- **Measured chain** (local CI-equivalent stack): PATCH `200` at about +150 ms; then a refresh RSC fetch and a navigation RSC fetch of the full page, alongside about 9 `<Link>` prefetches; the label changed only when the navigation RSC response arrived (about +200 ms locally).
- **Reproduced deterministically:** delaying the page's RSC responses by 12 s produced the identical failure ("element(s) not found", 11.1 s). The database showed the approval persisted (`client_review`, one `internal_approval_recorded` row) while the UI still offered "Internally approve preview".
- **Hypotheses tested and ruled out:**
  - navigation overtaking the refresh: both fetches start after the commit and return fresh data;
  - the Next 15.5.28 prefetch-cache aliasing path: it refetches page segments;
  - a refused transition: the gate inputs are deterministic for the fixture;
  - the Forge mutation rate limit: it is keyed per project path;
  - the service worker: it is network-only, `no-store`.
- **Not reproduced by repetition alone:** test 16 passed 20/20 in isolation and 10/10 in full-suite runs under 4-core load before the fix. The CI failure needs a slower server re-render than this machine produces, which is why the regression test injects the delay.

## Changes

- `admin/src/lib/forge-preview-decision.ts` (new, pure):
  - the decision available from a status;
  - strict reading of the persisted status from the PATCH response;
  - the display rule: a server-confirmed status applies only to the props snapshot it was confirmed against, and the next server render is authoritative again, including changes made elsewhere.
- `ForgeProjectDetail.tsx`:
  - every status-dependent read uses the effective status;
  - advances only on a recognised status returned by a successful PATCH, never optimistically;
  - an unconfirmed or failed response shows an error and does not advance;
  - a `useRef` guard means a double click records one decision (state-based guards read a stale closure within the same frame);
  - busy and completion states are announced through a polite `role="status"`, and errors keep the existing alert;
  - navigation is unchanged.
- `api/forge/projects/[id]/route.ts`: a status change is applied only `where status = <the status the transition was checked against>`; if it no longer matches, the route returns **409** `status_conflict`. Updates without a status change are unaffected.
- `scripts/test-database.mjs`: two new guarded fixtures, "E2E Approval Latency" and "E2E Approval Concurrency"; the asserted fixture count goes from 9 to 11.

# Operation Ascend (B2): architecture

Status: B2.1 implemented on `feature/operation-ascend-b2` (draft, switched off). B2.2 to B2.7 are designed here and **not started**.

## Reconciliation with the existing roadmap

`docs/expansion/intelligence/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` labels a different "B2" (Website Intelligence, "not started, security design required first"), followed by B3 Sales Studio, B4 meeting prep/proposals/handover, B5 Ask ScaleSmiths and B6 Support. That table is a roadmap label, not an approved specification, so Ascend adopts the B2 name as directed. Overlaps:

| Earlier label | Ascend slice that touches it | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| B2 Website Intelligence | none | Stays separate and not started. Ascend makes no website fetches (no SSRF surface). |
| B3 Sales Studio | B2.2 qualification | B2.2 is deterministic qualification over existing discovery fields; no generated content. |
| B4 Meeting prep, proposals, handover | B2.1 (meeting visibility), B2.6 (handoff) | B2.6 replaces the "handover" part of B4 if the founder agrees. |
| B5 Ask ScaleSmiths | B2.7 extension points | No live AI in B2. |
| B6 Support and operations | B2.3 command centre | B2.3 extends the B1.6 founder operations queue. |

**Founder decision FD-ASC-01:** confirm that Ascend's B2 supersedes the earlier B2–B6 numbering, or rename Ascend. Until then both labels are documented.

## Principles

1. **One source of truth per fact.** Opportunity stage: `expansion_opportunities.status`. Money: `expansion_payment_events`, `expansion_contracts`, commission ledger (`expansion-finance`). History: `expansion_audit` (append-only). Meetings: `expansion_meeting_requests`. Ascend reads these; it adds new tables only for genuinely new facts.
2. **No new authority paths.** Stage changes keep using `partnerMutation('stage')` (ownership + `PARTNER_TRANSITIONS` + commercial clearance). Founder decisions keep using `founderMutation`. Assistance requests use `requestMeeting`. UI gestures can only call these.
3. **Switched off by default**, one switch per slice (`PARTNER_PIPELINE_ENABLED`, then `FOUNDER_SALES_COMMAND_ENABLED`, `REVENUE_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED`, `DELIVERY_HANDOFF_ENABLED`, `ASCEND_AUTOMATION_ENABLED`).
4. **Derived before stored.** Columns, attention reasons, meeting state and timeline are computed per request from existing rows.

## Dependency graph

```text
B0–B1.6 (master) ──┬─ B2.1 pipeline ──┬─ B2.2 qualification ── B2.5 performance
                   │                  ├─ B2.3 command centre ─┬─ B2.6 delivery handoff
                   │                  │                        └─ B2.7 automation (needs B2.3 + B2.6)
                   └─ expansion-finance ── B2.4 revenue + forecast (needs only finance; independent of B2.1)
B1.7 (#163, unmerged) ── B2.3 (its founder queue additions should land first to avoid conflicts)
```

B2.4 can start in parallel with B2.1. B2.3 should wait for #163, which extends `founderOperations`.

## B2.1 design (implemented)

| Concern | Implementation |
|---|---|
| Pure model | `admin/src/lib/partner-pipeline.ts`: columns, meeting state, attention reasons, permitted/blocked transitions with reasons, partner-safe timeline projection, filtering and sorting |
| Server | `admin/src/lib/server/partner-pipeline.ts`: `partnerPipeline`, `partnerOpportunityDetail`, `recordInteraction`, `scheduleFollowUp` |
| API | `GET/POST /api/partner/pipeline` (same-origin JSON, durable rate limit 60/min) |
| Page | `/partner/pipeline` (board, table, compact list; detail dialog) |
| Storage | Migration `0098`: `expansion_opportunity_interactions` (append-only, owner-guard trigger). Follow-up uses the existing `prospects.next_follow_up_at`. |
| Reused | `PARTNER_TRANSITIONS`, `OPPORTUNITY_STATUS` copy, `partnerGuard`, `requestMeeting`, `ProspectGuidance` (B1.6, when its switch is on) |

Columns: New (registered, contacted) · Discovery (discovery, qualified, deferred) · Information required (more_information, bespoke_required) · With ScaleSmiths (scope_submitted) · Approved · Contract accepted · Closed (closed_lost, withdrawn). Every status maps to exactly one column (unit-tested).

Timeline sources: `expansion_audit` rows for the opportunity and its meetings, plus verification dates from `expansion_payment_events`. A whitelist maps actions to partner-safe labels; everything else (classification, market, exclusivity, discount, notes, amounts) is dropped.

## B2.2–B2.7 designs (not started)

- **B2.2 qualification:** extend `guidancePlanFor`/`discoveryGaps`; add an explainable checklist (factors shown, no weights hidden, no auto-reject). Duplicate detection: add a normalised-name trigram check behind the existing advisory lock (`pg_advisory_xact_lock(621908148)`); response stays the existing non-revealing 409.

- **B2.4 revenue:** read-only views over `expansion_payment_events` and the commission ledger; forecasts in a separate `expansion_forecast_scenarios` table that the finance engine never reads. No invented conversion rates: show "insufficient history" below a threshold the founder sets.

### OR-1 proposed correction (not applied)

Diagnose before changing anything, from a machine outside the hosting network:

```bash
dig +short admin.scalesmiths.co.uk A AAAA CNAME
curl -sSI https://admin.scalesmiths.co.uk/login | sed -n '1,12p'

Likely causes, in order: (1) the admin hostname's DNS record points at the host that serves Confirm a Kill and that host's default nginx `server` block answers with its redirect; (2) the admin `server_name` is missing from the admin nginx site, so the request falls to the default server; (3) a registrar-level URL forward. # Operation Ascend (B2): security model

Applies to B2.1 as implemented; later slices must extend this file before they ship.

## Boundaries

| Boundary | Enforcement (server-side) | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Feature off | `PARTNER_PIPELINE_ENABLED !== "true"` → page `notFound()`, API 404 before any query | `partner-pipeline.database.test.ts` "is off by default" |
| Identity | Middleware + `routeAccess` allow-list adds only `/partner/pipeline` (GET/HEAD) for `independent_partner`; API under existing `/api/partner/*` rule | `rbac.test.ts` |
| Active partner | `partnerGuard`: activated profile, active user, current `session_version`, partner role; failures → 403 | "refuses suspended partners and non-partner roles" |
| Ownership | Every read and write filters `partner_id = <own>`; research-allocated prospects only when allocated to that partner | "shows a partner only their own…", "treats another partner's opportunity exactly like a missing one" |
| Non-enumeration | Another partner's id, an unallocated research id, a random id and a malformed id all return the same 404 message | same test |
| Database ownership | `expansion_interaction_owner_guard` trigger rejects an interaction whose partner does not own the opportunity | "the database refuses…" |
| Append-only | `commercial_history_immutable` trigger on interactions | "records interactions append-only…" |
| Stage integrity | UI offers only `PARTNER_TRANSITIONS`; changes go through `partnerMutation('stage')`, which re-checks transition and commercial clearance | `partner-pipeline.test.ts` transitions |
| Timeline privacy | Whitelist projection drops founder notes, pricing, terms, sector/market/exclusivity, discount and suppression events; payment rows give dates only | "builds a partner-safe timeline" |
| Audit hygiene | `interaction_recorded` audit stores kind and id, never the note text | "audits without the text" |
| CSRF / size | `expansionBody`: same-origin, JSON only, 64 KiB cap | existing `expansion-http` coverage |
| Abuse | Durable rate limit 60 writes/min per partner on the pipeline API; meeting requests keep their own 10-open cap | code review |
| Rendering | Notes rendered as React text (no HTML), `white-space: pre-wrap` | "records interactions…" stores `<script>` verbatim; React escapes |
| Query bounds | Pipeline ≤ 500 opportunities, meetings ≤ 1000, detail timeline ≤ 200 audit rows, interactions ≤ 100 | code review |

## Threats considered

IDOR (covered by ownership + 404), SQL injection (parameterised `sql` template throughout; malformed id test), forged transitions (server-side `assertPartnerTransition`), tampered monetary values (B2.1 reads no amounts and writes none), unsafe note rendering (text only), information in logs (no logging added), notification abuse (no notifications sent by B2.1).

## Not covered yet

- Browser E2E of the role matrix (Journey E) — not written in this session.
- Founder visibility of interactions — none exists; FD-ASC-04.

## Summary

Operation Ascend B2.1: a partner pipeline over the existing, authoritative opportunity lifecycle, switched off by `PARTNER_PIPELINE_ENABLED`. Partners see only their own opportunities as a board, table or compact list with search, filters and sorting, and a detail view with a partner-safe history, meetings, an append-only interaction log, a private follow-up date and a founder-assistance request. Stage moves offer only `PARTNER_TRANSITIONS` and go through the existing `POST /api/partner` command, which re-checks ownership and commercial clearance; every other stage shows why it is unavailable. Also adds the B2 architecture, roadmap (with the B1 operational risk register and the proposed admin-redirect correction), security model, acceptance criteria and status under `docs/expansion/ascend/`.

## Type

- [x] `feat`
- [ ] `fix`
- [x] `test`
- [x] `docs`
- [ ] `refactor`
- [ ] `security`
- [ ] `perf`
- [ ] `chore`

## Scope

- [ ] Public web
- [x] Admin
- [ ] Forge
- [x] Database/migrations
- [ ] Docker/deployment/Nginx
- [ ] CI/tooling
- [ ] Documentation only

## Validation

Commands run, with results:

npx vitest run src/lib/partner-pipeline.test.ts src/lib/server/partner-pipeline.database.test.ts src/lib/rbac-authorization.test.ts  -> all pass (pipeline unit + 10 PGlite database cases)

npm run test:db:prepare && npm run test:db:migrate on disposable PostgreSQL 16.14                                                   -> "Shared migrations current: web 25/25, admin 99/99"; both 0098 triggers present
node scripts/check-migration-history.mjs                                                                                            -> "52 historical and 72 forward migrations are locked"
```

```text
Full admin unit suite locally: the machine was overloaded (5 s timeouts, a session crash); CI's Admin job is the authoritative run.
PostgreSQL 14 migration: started on a disposable postgres:14 container; result to be added as a PR comment.
Browser screenshots at 320-1920 px and Journey A/E Playwright specs: not written yet (see Residual Risk).
```

## Migrations

- [ ] No database migration.
- [x] Migration included and documented below.

`0098_ascend_pipeline_interactions`: forward-only and additive. New table `expansion_opportunity_interactions` (FKs to opportunity, partner and author; kind CHECK; summary 1-2000 chars), index `(opportunity_id, created_at desc)`, an insert trigger that refuses an interaction whose partner does not own the opportunity, and the existing `commercial_history_immutable` trigger (append-only). Registered in the Drizzle journal, `scripts/shared-migration-plan.json` and `scripts/migration-checksums.json`. The admin role already receives SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on all tables; no DELETE grant is needed. Not run against any non-local database.

## Environment

- [ ] No environment-variable change.
- [x] Environment variables added to `.env.example` and documented below.

`PARTNER_PIPELINE_ENABLED` (admin app, default `false`). Page and API return 404 and no navigation link appears while it is off.

## Security and Privacy

- [x] No secrets, provider credentials, real `.env` files, database dumps, or
      client-private exports are included.
- [x] Admin/Forge access control and generated-workspace isolation are preserved.
- [x] Public analytics remains minimised and consent-aware.

RBAC: `/partner/pipeline` added to the partner page allow-list (GET/HEAD only; nothing beneath it); new policy rule `ascend.pipeline` for `/api/partner/pipeline` (resource-owner scope). Another partner's opportunity, an unallocated research prospect, a random id and a malformed id all return the same 404. Suspended partners get 403. The history is a whitelist projection: founder review notes, pricing and terms, sector/market/exclusivity decisions, discount and suppression events and payment amounts are never returned. The audit entry for an interaction stores its kind and id, not its text. Notes render as React text. Full model: `docs/expansion/ascend/B2-SECURITY-MODEL.md`.

Database and RBAC tests listed above. Browser evidence not yet captured; this PR is a draft until it is.

Revert the commit. The switch is off, so nothing is reachable in production even if deployed. Migration 0098 is additive and nothing else reads the table, so the previous code runs on the migrated schema; per the forward-only policy there is no down-migration.

content.text:
B2.1 now has its browser evidence. A new Journey A and E browser test passes in CI against a production build and a disposable database. CI on the latest head (screenshots and docs only) is still running; the previous head was green apart from one Web job that was still running.

**What the test covers** (`admin/test/e2e/ascend-pipeline.spec.ts`, run by the existing Empower Browser Acceptance job):
- **Journey A:**
  - The registered prospect lands in the "New" column. Board, table and list views all work, and so do search, stage, "needs my action" and sort.
  - Keyboard: opening the detail dialog moves focus into it, Tab stays inside, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the card.
  - The partner can make only the allowed stage moves, and each other stage shows its reason.
  - Recording an interaction and setting a follow-up date work.
  - A founder-help request reaches the founder queue. The founder's confirmation shows up for the partner, without the founder's private note.
  - The commission ledger is unchanged.
- **Journey E:** another partner gets "not found" when reading, adding a note, setting a follow-up or forcing a stage change on Partner A's prospect. A partner cannot set "approved" on their own prospect. Founder-only pages, revoked sessions and anonymous requests are all refused, and the ledger is unchanged.
- **Accessibility:** axe (WCAG 2.2 AA, serious and critical) found no violations on the board, table or dialog. No page scrolls sideways at any width.

**Four problems the screenshots showed, now fixed:**
- The guidance panel inside the dialog kept showing "Registered" after the prospect moved to discovery; it now refreshes after a stage move.
- Meeting rows showed raw text such as "technical scoping / requested"; they now read "Technical scoping / Meeting requested".
- The summary cards touched the header block, and on phones they took one row each.
- The shared partner header cut off "SCALESMITHS" between 641 and 1100 px. That was already happening on the existing B1.6 pages, and the fix applies to them too.

I also made two smaller wording fixes: a backwards stage now gives a specific reason, and the "update discovery" link no longer breaks its sentence.

The 30 screenshots (board, table, list, dialog top and dialog history at 320, 390, 768, 1024, 1440 and 1920 px) are committed in `docs/expansion/ascend/evidence/b2-1/`. I looked at all of them after the last run. `B2-IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md`, the security model and the [#166](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/166) description now record this.

**Still not done:** no manual screen-reader pass, and reduced motion is only checked by reading the CSS. The Admin Forge E2E check failed once on #166 in the known intermittent test that #164 fixes, and passed on later heads.
